name: Pagination
purpose: Divide a large amount of content into pages and let users jump directly to any page, or step forward/backward.
intent: Provide a controlled, accessible page-range control: page-number buttons styled by ToggleButton's own stylesheet, IconButton for previous/next, with a reusable sibling/boundary-count windowing algorithm.

figmaSource.note: A single component (not a variant set), 512x32, demonstrating currentPage=1 of totalPages=20.

structure.pagePartWraps: toggle-button (size=sm (32), tone=subtle when unselected, isSelected true/false)
structure.ellipsisNote: Plain '...' text at color/content/subtle, no button wrapper - confirmed from the actual node tree, despite the component-search metadata describing it as a subtle Button.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's one demo (currentPage=1, totalPages=20) shows 12 consecutive pages before collapsing to an ellipsis + page 20 - a width-fitting demo, not a literal algorithm. The component instead implements the standard sibling+boundary-count windowing algorithm (getPaginationRange), which with default siblingCount=1/boundaryCount=1 renders '1 2 … 20' for the same inputs. A consumer can raise siblingCount to get a wider range closer to Figma's sample.

Figma's per-item VARIANT prop name 'tone' on both toggle-button and icon-button instances maps to this codebase's existing ToggleButtonTone/IconButtonAppearance prop values ('subtle'), not a new prop Pagination needs to invent.

Page numbers take ToggleButton's look (its stylesheet's toggleButton/size_sm/tone_subtle/selected classes on a native button) but not its semantics: ToggleButton always sets aria-pressed, and a page is a position, so the current page carries only aria-current="page".

antiPatterns: only one or two total pages

anatomy.description: Chevron-left control, disabled on the first page.
One per visible page number; selected look + aria-current="page" on the current page, no aria-pressed.
Non-interactive '...' text wherever the range algorithm collapses a gap.
Chevron-right control, disabled on the last page.

currentPage.description: 1-based current page, rounded down and clamped to 1..totalPages.

onPageChange.description: Called with the target page when a page/previous/next control is activated.

siblingCount.description: Pages shown on either side of the current page.

boundaryCount.description: Pages always shown at the start and end of the range.

getPageLabel.description: aria-label generator for each page button.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the nav landmark. Ignored when aria-labelledby is set.

aria-labelledby.description: Names the nav by the id of a visible heading, in place of aria-label.

ariaLabel.description: Deprecated alias for aria-label, still accepted.

className.description: Optional custom class name for the root nav.

requirements: nav must always have an accessible name (aria-label, default 'Pagination', or aria-labelledby).
The current page control must carry aria-current="page" and no aria-pressed, so it is announced once.
Previous/next must have accessible names and must be disabled at the first/last page; when the focused one becomes disabled, focus moves to the current page.
The ellipsis must be aria-hidden and non-interactive.

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves through previous, each visible page, and next in order; Enter/Space activates the focused control.
behaviorRules: Render exactly one IconButton for previous and one for next.
Render one page button (ToggleButton's look) per page number returned by getPaginationRange, plus a non-interactive ellipsis wherever the algorithm returns 'ellipsis'.
Mark the page button matching currentPage with the selected look and aria-current="page".
Round currentPage down and clamp it to 1..totalPages (1 when there are no pages).
When Previous or Next had focus and the new page disables it, move focus to the current page.
Forward other attributes and the ref to the root nav.
Disable previous when currentPage <= 1; disable next when currentPage >= totalPages.
Call onPageChange with the clicked page number, or currentPage -1 / currentPage + 1 for previous/next.
Default siblingCount=1, boundaryCount=1, aria-label='Pagination' (deprecated alias ariaLabel), previousLabel='Previous page', nextLabel='Next page'.
compositionRules: Pagination renders IconButton for previous/next, and page numbers as native buttons with ToggleButton's own stylesheet classes (not ToggleButton itself, which forces aria-pressed) - do not reimplement their visual states locally.
Use Progress Indicator instead of Pagination for step-based flow progress.
contentRules: Page numbers only - no custom per-page labels.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all color comes from ToggleButton/IconButton's own semantic tokens plus --color-content-subtle for the ellipsis.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, or typography.
getPaginationRange must be a pure function, exported for independent unit testing.
Reuse IconButton directly, and ToggleButton's stylesheet for page numbers, rather than reimplementing their styling.

Page buttons are a fixed --size-control-sm square (instead of ToggleButton's content-based width) through Pagination's own `.page` class; ToggleButton sets no inline-size, so there is nothing to out-specify.
do: Use for a paged table, list, or search-results view.
Keep the consumer in control of currentPage via onPageChange.
Raise siblingCount/boundaryCount for a wider visible range.
dont: Do not use for infinite scroll / load more content.
Do not use for step-based flow progress.
Do not use with only one or two total pages.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders previous, the computed page range (with ellipses), and next.
getPaginationRange produces the documented output for small ranges, middle-of-range, near-start, and near-end cases.
Clicking a page number calls onPageChange with that page.
Clicking previous/next calls onPageChange with currentPage -1/+1.
Previous is disabled on page 1; next is disabled on the last page.
The current page has aria-current="page" and no page sets aria-pressed.
currentPage is clamped; focus moves to the current page when a focused Previous/Next is disabled.
nav has an accessible name, defaulting to 'Pagination'.
Tests cover the range algorithm directly plus rendering/interaction/accessibility.
knownLimitations: The ellipsis is not interactive - matches the literal Figma node, and does not yet expose which pages it collapsed.
Does not measure container width to decide how many pages to show.
futureEnhancements: The ellipsis becomes a Dropdown Menu (organism) trigger listing the hidden page numbers - intentionally deferred until Dropdown Menu exists in this design system, so Pagination doesn't depend on an unbuilt organism. getPaginationRange will need to return which pages each 'ellipsis' collapsed, not just the marker, to support this.
